english: Consider the ellipse $E:\dfrac{x^{2}}{4}+y^{2}=1$. Let $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$ be the circles with centres $\left(-\dfrac{3}{10},0\right)$ and $\left(\dfrac{6}{5},0\right)$ respectively, each of which touches $E$ at two distinct points. Then the length of the common chord of $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$ is ______.
hindi: दीर्घवृत्त $E:\dfrac{x^{2}}{4}+y^{2}=1$ पर विचार कीजिए। माना कि $C_{1}$ तथा $C_{2}$ क्रमशः केन्द्रों $\left(-\dfrac{3}{10},0\right)$ तथा $\left(\dfrac{6}{5},0\right)$ वाले वे वृत्त हैं जिनमें से प्रत्येक $E$ को दो भिन्न बिन्दुओं पर स्पर्श करता है। तब $C_{1}$ तथा $C_{2}$ की उभयनिष्ठ जीवा की लम्बाई ______ है।
solution: At a point of contact the radius is a common normal of the circle and $E$, so the centre lies on the normal of $E$

$C_{2}$: $h=\dfrac65$, $x_{0}=\dfrac85$, $y_{0}^{2}=1-\dfrac{16}{25}=\dfrac{9}{25}$, $r_{2}^{2}=\left(\dfrac25\right)^{2}+\dfrac{9}{25}=\dfrac{13}{25}$ (the two points $(x_{0},\pm y_{0})$ give double contact)
Distance of the chord from the centre of $C_{2}$ is $\dfrac35$, so length $=2\sqrt{\dfrac{13}{25}-\dfrac{9}{25}}=\dfrac45$
solution_full: If a circle with centre $K(h,0)$ touches $E$ at $Q$, then the circle and $E$ have the same tangent at $Q$, so they also have the same normal there; the normal of the circle at $Q$ is the line $QK$. Hence $K$ lies on the normal of $E$ at $Q$.

For $E$: $a=2$, $b=1$, $e^{2}=1-\dfrac14=\dfrac34$. The normal at $Q(2\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ is $\dfrac{2x}{\cos\theta}-\dfrac{y}{\sin\theta}=4-1=3$ (for $\sin\theta\neq0$). It meets the $x$-axis at $x=\dfrac32\cos\theta=\dfrac34x_{0}$, where $x_{0}=2\cos\theta$.

So a circle centred at $(h,0)$ touching $E$ at points off the axis touches it at $(x_{0},\pm y_{0})$ with $x_{0}=\dfrac43h$ (two distinct points, which needs $|x_{0}|<2$). A circle touching $E$ only at a vertex $(\pm2,0)$ touches it at one point only, so the circles in the question are these.

Check of the double contact: $C_{2}-E$ in the form $\left(x-\dfrac65\right)^{2}+y^{2}-\dfrac{13}{25}-\left(\dfrac{x^{2}}{4}+y^{2}-1\right)=\dfrac34\left(x-\dfrac85\right)^{2}$, a perfect square, so the common chord of $C_{2}$ and $E$ is the doubled line $x=\dfrac85$; similarly $C_{1}-E=\dfrac34\left(x+\dfrac25\right)^{2}$.
The circles meet, since the distance between centres $\dfrac32$ lies between $r_{1}-r_{2}$ and $r_{1}+r_{2}\approx1.71$.

Common chord of $C_{1}$ and $C_{2}$: subtracting the equations, $\left(x+\dfrac{3}{10}\right)^{2}-\left(x-\dfrac65\right)^{2}=\dfrac{97}{100}-\dfrac{52}{100}$, i.e. $\dfrac32\left(2x-\dfrac{9}{10}\right)=\dfrac{9}{20}$, so $3x-\dfrac{27}{20}=\dfrac{9}{20}$ and $x=\dfrac35$.

The distance of this line from the centre of $C_{2}$ is $\dfrac65-\dfrac35=\dfrac35$, so the length of the common chord is $2\sqrt{r_{2}^{2}-\dfrac{9}{25}}=2\sqrt{\dfrac{4}{25}}=\dfrac45=0.8$. (End points $\left(\dfrac35,\pm\dfrac25\right)$.)
originality_note: New: circles of double contact with an ellipse, located through the common normal (the centre is where the normal at the contact point meets the major axis, at e^2 x0), and then their radical axis and its length (way 5, the link between the common normal and the circles' common chord). Closest known: the normal of an ellipse meets the major axis at e^2 x1; common chord of two given circles. Different because: the circles are not given by equations but by double contact, so the common normal must be used to find them before the common chord.
key_step: Use the common normal at a contact point: the centre (h,0) lies on the normal at the point with x0 = h/e^2, which gives each radius; then subtract the circle equations.
justification: Two ideas linked: the normal of an ellipse meeting the axis at e^2 x0 (via the common normal of circle and ellipse), then the common chord of two circles and its length, in numerical form with exact fractions. Comparable to 2023-P2-Q13 in style but with a more familiar key step, so 3; nearest 2023-P1-Q2 (L3).
stem_review: Read as a student: every curve, point and parameter is introduced, the conditions are complete, there is one reading, the answer is unique and equals the Answer Plan, and the Hindi mirrors the English. Checked that each centre gives exactly one circle touching E at two distinct points (the circles touching at a vertex touch at one point), that C1 and C2 intersect, and that the chord length is exact. Answer 0.80, a decimal between 0 and 1. No change.
